parsed.draft_response:
Apologies for the trouble—especially given the Monday launch deadline. I can see why this is urgent.

Since the restore was initiated within the retention window but you’re still seeing missing files and comments, we’ll need to investigate the specific project restore result and exactly what content is absent.

To help our engineering team review it quickly, could you please reply with:
1) The workspace/project location in our product (product/module name or where the project lives).
2) Approximate deletion time (date + time and time zone) and the time the restore was initiated (and completed, if you have it).
3) Confirmation of what you saw when clicking restore (any success message/status, and any timestamps).
4) Which items are missing: list the specific files and/or comment threads (names/IDs/URLs if available).
5) Whether there were multiple restore attempts and whether any errors or warnings appeared.
6) Whether anything else besides files/comments is missing (e.g., project metadata, permissions, attachments).

In the meantime, please avoid repeated restore/delete actions for the same project until we review your details, as that can complicate the investigation.

We’ve escalated this for human review so engineering can check what happened during restore and advise on the next best step. Reply with the details above and we’ll continue as quickly as possible.
promised_actions: Escalate the case for human review by engineering
Review the restore outcome and the specific missing files/comments once the requested details are provided
safety_notes: Do not promise restoration completion, refund, or root cause; user reports missing content after restore and requires engineering investigation.
Avoid claiming any specific technical determination until investigation is completed.
